coaching.headline: We won zero fights to their five, and they cashed four of those. Four lanes favored on paper turned into a loss in 25 minutes with the tower count 0-6.
coaching.team: Our pre-game read gave us four of five lanes, with carry, mid, jungle and support all favored, and the early game backed it up. Xeebs opened with first blood on Kallari at 2.3. At 10, Crunch and Scarlett traded 1-for-1 deep in their half, and the first Fangtooth fell to us at 11 — a real cross-map trade and the best macro of the game. Then it unraveled on numbers. The fight at 14.6 in their half, lost 0-2, was taken while support, jungle and carry were all elsewhere. The fight at their Fangtooth at 16.9, lost 1-2, was two of ours into three while Countess and Drongo were alive, ahead in lane, and absent. Fangtooth fell at 17.6. From 19 minutes on, every fight was at their towers and every one was lost. The fight at 19 went 2-4, and the outer tower fell at 19.6 with the inner right behind. At 21.3, three of ours died 0-3 to just Sparrow and Renna, and Fangtooth followed at 22.6. The last try at 23.4 went 1-4. And the 23-minute Fangtooth fell uncontested with all five of us alive — a map-awareness problem, not a numbers problem. Next game: nobody starts a fight near a major until mid and carry have shoved and started walking.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: What was the plan at their Fangtooth at 16.9? Kwang and Scarlett took a two-man fight into three while Countess and Drongo, both alive and ahead in lane, never left their lanes. The fight was lost 1-2 and Fangtooth fell at 17.6. The teamfight that followed at their outer tower at 19 went 2-4. Three towers fell in the two minutes after it, from 19.6 to 20.8. That stretch turned an even Fangtooth count into their game.

perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster's cross-map read at 10 was right: a 1-for-1 trade deep in their half while the 11-minute Fangtooth fell to us. The rest of the map went the other way. Scarlett was alive but never joined the fight at 14.6, lost 0-2. And every one of Scarlett's deaths came shortly before a tower or Fangtooth fell — the death at 17.1 was followed by Fangtooth at 17.6, and that pattern held all game. When a fight starts near a major, Scarlett arriving is worth more than any camp.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim won the lane on paper, but the map never saw the lead. Drongo was alive and ahead while the fights at 14.6 and 16.9 were being lost. The death at 19 came just before the outer tower fell at 19.6, with the inner right after. The death at 21.3 was followed by Fangtooth at 22.6. And two completed items in 25 minutes meant the late fights ran without the win condition online: Tainted Rounds, the third piece of the 58.1% Lightning Hawk, Vanquisher and Tainted Rounds core, was never built.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs took first blood on Kallari at 2.3 and killed Murdock again at 10 in the Fangtooth trade. Then it went back one pick at a time: caught alone by the same Murdock three times between 6.9 and 18, with only 2 wards placed all game and no armor bought into a three-physical comp. Those death timers opened the river, and it went 16 buffs to our 6.

7682f9ea-ae1d-42fe-adf4-89bf55b76e97.text: Countess held the one mid matchup that was ours on paper and returned 0/3/0 with zero objective damage. No rotation came to the Fangtooth fight next door at 16.9 — a won lane left in the lane.

b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.text: Kwang did the support job: 12 wards, the kill on Riktor at 8.1 deep in our jungle, and a body in nearly every fight. Six deaths is what being the only one who kept showing up looks like.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.text: Every one of Scarlett's four deaths was followed by a falling tower or Fangtooth. The first cost the outer tower at 11.6, the second the Fangtooth at 17.6. The last two were followed by the Fangtooth at 22.6 and the inner tower at 24.5. The jungle's deaths were the most expensive on the team.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.text: Drongo was ahead in lane and absent from both mid-game fights that decided the map, the one at 14.6 and the one at their Fangtooth at 16.9. The lead never left the lane, so the team never had it.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.text: First blood at 2.3, then three solo deaths to the same Murdock before minute 18, on 2 wards. That was the one lane our read called unfavored, and it was handed over in the fog.

coaching.whatWorked: The trade at 10 deep in their half was the one true cross-map play of the game: Crunch and Scarlett committed across the map while the first Fangtooth fell to us at 11. Bodies went where the objective was the prize — that read held up and is the piece to keep.

19.call: With Fangtooth just lost at 17.6, what did a five-man engage at their outer tower win even if it went perfectly? The reset was the play: group on our own side, hold for the next spawn, and take the fight where their walk is the long one.

23.4.call: What changed since the fight lost at their outer tower at 19 to make a third try at the same walls the right call? Nothing had. After two collapses on that ground, the play was to stop knocking, set up at our own structures, and make them start the next fight into us.

21.3.call: Why trade at their outer tower with a Fangtooth spawn live on the map? The objective was the prize of that window, and it stood across the map while three of ours committed to the walls. The play was to set up on the spawn with vision and let them start the fight into us.

7682f9ea-ae1d-42fe-adf4-89bf55b76e97.build: Countess kept Noxia, whose mark adds a chunk of the target's maximum health when a second ability lands, but the rest of the core never arrived in a two-item game. Combustion adds area burst to every combo and Wraith Leggings adds magic penetration, the difference between chunking the Renna trade and winning it. Flux Matrix at least brought magic resist, yet the flag in the facts points the other way: no armor against a lineup whose main damage was Murdock's 27k physical.
7682f9ea-ae1d-42fe-adf4-89bf55b76e97.eternal: Vesh suits Countess's dive pattern: she blinks in, dumps abilities, and the burn keeps working while she resets. The Tenth Seal loads extra power into her level-10 ultimate, the centerpiece of her all-in, and Mind Rot lets the burn hurt tankier targets too. What it gives up is staying power in the melee she lands in; the loadout adds no toughness or lifesteal, so the all-in has to finish the job before the enemy answers.

b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.build: Kwang's two finished items split the difference: Golem's Gift stacks armor that his constant casting keeps refreshed, and Tainted Scepter cuts the target's healing, which had a real job against a Kallari who healed 11,126 health. The skipped pieces, Spirit Of Amir and Oathkeeper, are the damage half of his core: raw magic power plus an empowered strike after every cast, the mechanic that turns his ability loops into real trades. With 13,022 hero damage and six deaths, the defensive lean neither kept him alive nor made him dangerous; the empowered-attack core at least makes the same casts threaten somebody.
b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.eternal: Vesh works with how Kwang fights: every ability that connects leaves a burn, and his kit cycles abilities constantly in melee range. Mind Rot adds current-health damage so the burn matters against frontliners, and The Tenth Seal boosts his level-10 ultimate. The trade-off is that a support Kwang gets no peel, healing, or toughness from it; this is a loadout for a Kwang who initiates and brawls, and it leaves protecting the carry entirely to his items and positioning.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Cuban Noobster's Tainted Blade earned its slot: the healing cut had a target in Kallari's 11,126 health healed, and its Hex makes the marked enemy take extra damage from everyone. Alternator is a scaling pick, boosting Scarlett's alternate casts and evolving later, and in a 25-minute loss that later never came. The bigger gap was defensive: the facts flag no armor against a three-physical lineup, and 26,260 damage taken against 7,588 dealt is the profile of a jungler who could not stay in the fights she joined.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Thraex fits Scarlett's brawling kit: her damage comes from staying glued to one target, and the mark makes that target both take more from her and deal less back. Ferocity's stacking attack speed rewards exactly the long, grinding exchanges she wants, with Savage Strikes adding on-hit sting from the first swing. It gives up burst and any team-wide utility; if a fight is a quick poke-and-retreat, the loadout barely turns on.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Willy Guggenheim had two-thirds of Drongo's winning core: Vanquisher's crit, penetration, and execute, plus Lightning Hawk's slowing empowered shots. The absent third was Tainted Rounds, which cuts enemy healing on every hit and hits harder the lower the target falls, made for shutting down a Kallari who healed 11,126 health across the game. In a 25-minute loss that ended at two finished items the order was defensible; the anti-heal was the piece this lineup specifically rewarded, and it stayed on the shelf.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Vermis is built for Drongo's job: every third basic attack on the same enemy adds max-health damage, so his sustained fire threatens tanks and squishies alike. Serration finishes the proc with missing-health damage and Melting Point keeps armor stackers honest. The cost is that nothing in it protects him or speeds his escape; it assumes the team buys him the uninterrupted attacking time it needs.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Xeebs's Augmentation and Mutilator are the right damage engine for Crunch: an empowered punch after each ability, plus max-health chunks on every combo. Tainted Blade, the skipped core piece, adds a healing cut and a mark that makes the target take more damage, and it carries health besides. The sharper issue was the flag in the facts: no armor into a three-physical lineup led by Murdock's 27k, the same Murdock who caught Crunch alone three times; an armor piece turns some of those catches into escapes.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Thraex matches the Murdock lane: Crunch wants long boxing matches, and the mark means his target takes more damage while dealing him less, softening exactly the ranged trades Murdock leans on. Ferocity ramps his attack speed the longer he stays in contact, feeding more ability procs. It trades away burst and escape; when Murdock keeps range and refuses the brawl, the blessing sits idle, which makes closing the gap the whole game plan.

Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

loadout.name: Sting Operation
loadout.text: Murdock gains 2 additional Max Static Trap Charges and Static Traps are 20% larger.

ability.name: Static Trap
ability.what: Place a trap that arms after a short delay, dealing 40/80/120/160/200 (+100%)(+120%) magical damage to any Enemy Hero that steps on it and Rooting them for 1.25s.

loadout.plain: More Static Trap charges and larger traps. Seed bushes, objectives and escape routes with roots to protect yourself and set up picks.

loadout.name: Vermis
loadout.text: Every 3rd consecutive Basic Attack on the same Enemy Hero within 2.5s deals 3% (+0.25% per Level) of their Max Health as bonus Physical Damage.
loadout.plain: Every third basic attack on the same hero adds damage based on their max health. Murdock's basic-attack focus makes this a steady boost, best into tanks.

loadout.name: Serration
loadout.text: Vermis also deals 3.5% of the target's Missing Health as bonus Physical Damage.
loadout.plain: Adds missing-health damage on top of Vermis procs, helping finish hurt targets.

loadout.name: Melting Point
loadout.text: Deal 10% bonus damage to targets with more than 125 Physical Armor.
loadout.plain: Extra damage only into enemies with over 125 physical armor. Buckshot's shred lowers their armor and can drop them below that line, so this is a pick into heavy tanks only.

loadout.name: Liberator
loadout.text: Purifying Guard:  Cleanse all Debuffs. Gain a 80 (+100%) Shield for 2.5s.
loadout.plain: Removes slows, stuns and other debuffs and gives a short shield. Save it for when you get caught, then Hot Pursuit away or keep shooting.

loadout.name: Sun Shards
loadout.text: Sparrow's basic attacks ricochet 1/2/3/4 times, dealing (+20%) Damage and applying On-Hit effects at 35% effectiveness.
loadout.plain: Basic attacks bounce to extra enemies, dealing reduced damage and applying on-hit item effects at 35% strength. Good for clearing waves and hitting grouped enemies.

loadout.name: Weald
loadout.text: Damaging an Enemy Hero below 30% Health fires 4 (+1 per 30% Bonus Attack Speed) projectiles that each deal 7 (+1 per level) True Damage. Missiles travel through walls and disappear after 3000u. 10s cooldown per Hero. On-hit effects apply at 20% effectiveness.
loadout.plain: Hitting a hero below 30% health fires missiles that pass through walls, with more missiles from bonus attack speed, which she builds a lot of. Helps finish low enemies running away.

loadout.name: Forage
loadout.text: Gain 3 additional Gold and 3 additional XP per Minion or Monster kill.
loadout.plain: Extra gold and experience from every minion and monster kill. Generic farming boost, nothing special with her kit.

loadout.name: Wind-Rider
loadout.text: Gain 15% (+1% per Level) Bonus Attack Speed for 4s after using a Dash, Leap, Teleport, or upon leaving Stealth.
loadout.plain: Leaving stealth after Heightened Senses gives extra attack speed on top of what the ability already grants, so that damage window hits even faster.

loadout.name: Pacifier
loadout.text: Adrenalize:  Dash a short distance. Empower your next Physical Damage Instance within 3s. Deals 30 (+25%) Damage. Increased by 2.5x against Targets below 20% Max Health. Killing a Hero within 3s allows Adrenalize to be recast for 6s.
loadout.plain: Dash and empower her next hit, which hits much harder on low-health targets and can be recast after a kill. Use it to finish someone softened by Piercing Shot.

lines: Lead story: Hard to kill. Died 1 time in 25 minutes, fewer deaths than about 94% of Sparrow carry players this patch. The build added healing off damage.
Sparrow dealt 23,898 hero damage, 26% of their team's, with +142 physical power from items.
Lightning Hawk (item): While moving or landing Basic Attacks: Generate stacks of Momentum. At 100 stacks empower your next Basic Attack On-Hit. Deal 40 (+20%) Damage. Slows by 20% for 0.75s.
Storm Breaker (item): While moving or landing Basic Attacks: Generate stacks of Momentum. At 100 stacks empower your next Basic Attack On-Hit. Release a bolt of lightning that chains to 7 Targets.
Sky Splitter (item): On Successful Basic Attacks: Deal 5% of Target's Current Health as Damage On-Hit. Reduced to 3.5% for Ranged Heroes. Minimum of 12 Damage.
Pacifier (crest): Dash a short distance. Empower your next Physical Damage Instance within 3s. Deals 30 (+25%) Damage. Increased by 2.5x against Targets below 20% Max Health.
Weald (Eternal): Damaging an Enemy Hero below 30% Health fires 4 (+1 per 30% Bonus Attack Speed) projectiles that each deal 7 (+1 per level) True Damage.
Sun Shards (augment): Sparrow's basic attacks ricochet 1/2/3/4 times, dealing (+20%) Damage and applying On-Hit effects at 35% effectiveness.
Sustain: 14% lifesteal; 1,450 healing recorded.

[7 + 1 a level: 21 at level 14] Field: 50.8% in 8217 games, 56% of picks, level the hero-role's 49.9%.

Loadout minor Forage: Extra gold and experience from every minion and monster kill. Generic farming boost, nothing special with her kit. (game text: Gain 3 additional Gold and 3 additional XP per Minion or Monster kill.) Field: 51.8% in 6085 games, 74% of picks, above the hero-role's 49.9%.

Loadout minor Wind-Rider: Leaving stealth after Heightened Senses gives extra attack speed on top of what the ability already grants, so that damage window hits even faster. (game text: Gain 15% (+1% per Level) Bonus Attack Speed for 4s after using a Dash, Leap, Teleport, or upon leaving Stealth.) Field: 50.9% in 6169 games, 75% of picks, above the hero-role's 49.9%.

Loadout crest Pacifier: Dash and empower her next hit, which hits much harder on low-health targets and can be recast after a kill. Use it to finish someone softened by Piercing Shot. (game text: Adrenalize:  Dash a short distance. Empower your next Physical Damage Instance within 3s. Deals 30 (+25%) Damage. Increased by 2.5x against Targets below 20% Max Health. Killing a Hero within 3s allows Adrenalize to be recast for 6s.) Field: 52.4% in 4919 games, 33% of picks, above the hero-role's 49.9%.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 5 effects on one trigger: Lightning Hawk, Storm Breaker, Sky Splitter, Weald, Sun Shards.
Stack (Healing off the damage): 2 effects on one trigger: Sky Splitter, Pacifier.
The Eternal was part of it: Weald (Forage + Wind-Rider) sits on the same trigger as the items (every basic attack set off), so the same hits paid out twice.
Countered? 1 of the 3 players Sparrow killed built physical armor (Kwang). Anti-heal on Kwang, Scarlett. We killed Sparrow 1 time.
Copy it? Weald (Forage + Wind-Rider): 51.6% in 4,755 Sparrow carry games, above the hero's 49.9%. Proven this patch: worth copying.
